title: Atomic Habits
alternate_titles: Atomic Habits: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones

contents: The Fundamentals: small changes, systems and identity-based habits
The 1st Law, Make It Obvious: cues, habit scoring, implementation intentions, stacking and environment
The 2nd Law, Make It Attractive: anticipation, temptation bundling, social norms and reframing
The 3rd Law, Make It Easy: repetition, friction, the two-minute rule and commitment devices
The 4th Law, Make It Satisfying: immediate rewards, tracking, recovery and accountability
Advanced Tactics: ability, motivation, mastery, review and the downside of automatic habits

audiences: Readers who understand a desired change but struggle to repeat it
People who want a practical system for starting or stopping simple recurring behaviours
Managers, coaches and designers who can change cues, friction and feedback
Readers of The Power of Habit who want a more operational guide

sources.title: Atomic Habits
sources.supports: Title, author, first US hardcover date, publisher, ISBN, 320-page extent, formats and stated aims.
sources.limitations: Authoritative for its edition; sales language and endorsements are promotional.

sources.title: Atomic Habits: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones
sources.supports: Full title, 2018 publication, ebook ISBN, pagination, selected contents and recurring concepts.
sources.limitations: Catalogue plus a limited authorised preview, not independent evaluation.

sources.title: Atomic Habits: Tiny Changes, Remarkable Results
sources.supports: The author's statement of the book's purpose, systems emphasis, one-percent framing, applications and intended audience.
sources.limitations: Sales page written by the author.

sources.title: Atomic Habits Summary
sources.supports: Authorised account of small improvements, identity, the habit loop, four laws and the main tactics.
sources.limitations: The author's compressed presentation, not a critical source.

sources.title: Psychology of Habit
sources.author_or_publisher: Wendy Wood and Dennis Rünger, Annual Review of Psychology
sources.supports: The research basis for habits as context-linked responses formed through repetition and their relationship with deliberate goals.
sources.limitations: General scientific review published before the book, not a test of Clear's complete package.

sources.title: Time to Form a Habit: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Health Behaviour Habit Formation and Its Determinants
sources.supports: Current evidence that stable contexts and repetition support automaticity, which usually takes months and varies substantially by person and behaviour.
sources.limitations: Focused on health behaviours; included studies and measures were heterogeneous.

sources.title: Making health habitual: the psychology of habit-formation and general practice
sources.author_or_publisher: Benjamin Gardner, Phillippa Lally and Jane Wardle, British Journal of General Practice
sources.supports: Practical evidence for simple actions repeated in consistent contexts, gradual automaticity and the finding that one missed opportunity does not materially derail formation.
sources.limitations: Short health-practice article, not a comprehensive review of every habit domain.

sources.title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes
sources.author_or_publisher: Peter Gollwitzer and Paschal Sheeran, Advances in Experimental Social Psychology
sources.supports: The research basis for if-then plans specifying when, where and how a goal-directed action will occur.
sources.limitations: Meta-analysis of implementation intentions, not the entire four-law framework.

sources.title: A systematic review on the effect of identity-related interventions on physical activity and smoking
sources.author_or_publisher: van Vliet et al., European Journal of Public Health
sources.supports: Identity-related interventions are plausible and promising, but results across physical activity and smoking studies are mixed.
sources.limitations: Conference-supplement systematic review of two health behaviours; it does not test Clear's specific identity-vote formulation.

sources.title: Book Review No. 4: Atomic Habits
sources.author_or_publisher: Lt Richard Pooley, British Army Centre for Army Leadership
sources.supports: Independent account of the identity and four-law structure, praise for accessibility and environmental design, and criticism of repetition and anecdotal support.
sources.limitations: One practitioner's military-context review, not scientific peer review.

sources.title: A Psychological Perspective on Behaviour Change: A Critical Analysis of Atomic Habits
sources.author_or_publisher: Alisha Fatima and Deepanjana Chakraborty, International Journal of Social Impact
sources.supports: A later psychological review finding that the four laws align with established ideas while omitting structural and cultural influences on behaviour.
sources.limitations: Recent low-citation review in a broad journal; useful as a named critique, not decisive evidence.

workflow.coverage_notes: Structure and core techniques checked against the authorised preview and author's summary; empirical claims checked against habit, implementation-intention and identity-intervention reviews; reception checked independently. No user-supplied full text was available.
